A certain company produces three types of cars: Standard, Sports, and Deluxe. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between the three types of cars each year:

|  |  | From: |  |  |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
|  |  | **Standard** | **Sports** | **Deluxe** |
| To: | **Standard** | $0.6$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ |
| **Sports** | $0.2$ | $0.6$ | $0.2$ |  |
| **Deluxe** | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.7$ |  |

For example, $20%$ of Standard customers switch to Sports each year, and $30%$ of Sports customers switch to Deluxe.

Currently, $500000$ customers use Standard, $400000$ customers use Sports and $100000$ customers use Deluxe. How many customers will use Sports in one year? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.

> A calculator is required to answer this question.

A certain company produces two types of smartphones: Phone $A$ and Phone $B.$ The following table describes how the number of customers changes between both types of smartphones each year:

|  |  | From: |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Phone $A$** | **Phone $B$** |
| To: | **Phone $A$** | $0.6$ | $0.3$ |
| **Phone $B$** | $0.4$ | $0.7$ |  |

That is, $40%$ of Phone $A$ customers switch to Phone $B$ each year, and $30%$ of Phone $B$ customers switch to Phone $A.$

Currently, $600\,000$ customers use Phone $A,$ while $400\,000$ customers use Phone $B.$ How many customers will use Phone $A$ in one year? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.

A certain company produces two types of motorcycles: classic and high-cylinder. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between both types of motorcycles each decade:

|  |  | From: |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Classic** | **High-Cylinder** |
| To: | **Classic** | $0.6$ | $0.2$ |
| **High-Cylinder** | $0.4$ | $0.8$ |  |

That is, $40%$ of classic motorcycle customers switch to high-cylinder each decade, and $20%$ of high-cylinder motorcycle customers switch to Classic.

Currently, $7\,000$ customers use classic motorcycles while $3\,000$ customers use high-cylinder motorcycles. How many customers will use high-cylinder motorcycles in one decade? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.

A certain company produces three types of milk: whole, skim, and lactose-free. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between the three types of milk each year:

|  |  | From: |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Whole** | **Skim** | **Lactose-free** |
| To: | **Whole** | $0.5$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ |
| **Skim** | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $0.4$ |  |
| **Lactose-free** | $0.2$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ |  |

For example, $30%$ of whole milk customers switch to skim milk each year, and $20%$ of lactose-free milk customers switch to whole milk.

Currently, $400\,000$ customers consume whole milk, $400\,000$ customers consume skim milk, and $200\,000$ customers consume lactose-free milk. How many customers will consume whole milk after one year? You may assume that the total number of customers doesn't change.

|  |  | From: |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

A certain company produces two types of footwear: casual and sports. The following table describes how the number of customers changes between both types of footwear each year:

|  |  | From: |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  | **Casual** | **Sports** |
| To: | **Casual** | $0.55$ | $0.7$ |
